name: MiDBD (TeO2)
summary: MiDBD, also called MiBeta in historical double-beta literature, was the 20-crystal tellurium bolometer programme preceding CUORICINO. It is distinct from the rhenium-187 MiBeta neutrino-mass experiment.
detection_principle: Tellurium dioxide crystals act as source and cryogenic calorimeter. A double-beta decay deposits heat; anticoincidence between crystals rejects multi-site backgrounds near the tellurium-130 endpoint.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The final 20-detector analysis reported no neutrinoless-decay signal and a 130Te half-life lower limit of 2.1 x 10^23 yr at 90% confidence.

collaboration.name: MiDBD (TeO2) Collaboration

key_parameters.name: Final 130Te limit
key_parameters.value: T1/2 greater than 2.1 x 10^23 yr, 90% confidence

results.summary: The final 20-detector analysis reported no neutrinoless-decay signal and a 130Te half-life lower limit of 2.1 x 10^23 yr at 90% confidence.

science_scope: A neutrinoless decay would violate lepton number. Half-life sensitivity is a forecast unless explicitly reported as an experimental limit; its interpretation as an effective Majorana mass depends on the decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements.
